Business E2E map

Personas and journeys first, then the feature catalog. Sources: ../upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging (98ee1b4), its route-posture snapshot lib/api/route-capability-coverage.snapshot.json (107 handlers), the page tree under app/, and the sibling maps. Flow internals live in business-data-context (cited by section id); endpoint semantics in business-api-context.

Overview

Four personas, the full MemberRole set, ranked by ROLE_RANK (lib/workspaces/invites.ts): owner 4, admin 3, member 2, viewer 1. Plus non-human callers: AI agents and CI with a PAT.

Top journeys

  • Author to run: story, ACs, ATC, Test, Run, verdict. The product's core loop.
  • Bug from a failed step: QA context carried into the defect.
  • Onboarding and invite: how anyone gets in.
  • Upgrade to Cloud: the only place money changes hands.
  • Delete and restore a workspace and export data: irreversible-data journeys.

Persona: Workspace Owner

Role: owner, one per workspace (workspaces.owner_user_id); every workspace creator. Goals: stand up the tenant, govern access, pay for the plan, own the data (export, delete, restore). Pain points: cannot leave as sole owner (isSoleOwner, lib/account/workspaces.ts); invite accept never demotes (reject_already_member). Test account: STAGING_OWNER_EMAIL / _PASSWORD (optional keys in .env.example). Journeys: onboarding, invite, upgrade, export, delete/restore, plus everything a member does.

Persona: Workspace Admin

Role: admin. Goals: onboard teammates (invite viewer/member/admin, never owner), issue scoped tokens, upgrade the plan, run the QA process. Pain points: cannot grant owner; cannot delete, restore or export the workspace. Test account: STAGING_ADMIN_EMAIL. Journeys: invite, upgrade, author-and-run.

Persona: QA Engineer (Member)

Role: member, the default authoring role. Goals: write stories and ACs, build reusable ATCs, compose Tests and Test Plans, run them, file bugs in context. Pain points (messages): "Every acceptance criterion must belong to the given user story." (45020); "This run is already closed and cannot accept new step results." (45212); "A bug must move to '<next>' first." (45310); "You must be a member of this workspace with write access." (42501). Test account: STAGING_MEMBER_EMAIL (the generic STAGING_USER_EMAIL carries no role guarantee). Journeys: author-and-run, bug-from-failure, test-plan, jira-import.

Persona: Viewer / Stakeholder

Role: viewer, read-only. Goals: follow coverage, traceability, run history and defects before a release call. Pain points: write controls are structurally absent (e.g. "Report bug" not rendered), and an API write returns the same "member with write access" message a non-member gets. Test account: STAGING_VIEWER_EMAIL. Journeys: read-only views of every journey.

Persona: AI agent / CI pipeline

Acts as the issuing member through a PAT (atc:read, atc:write, run:execute; workspace:admin only when explicitly issued). Can author ATCs, start runs and mark steps through the same API. Refused on cookie-only surfaces: token issue/revoke, active-workspace switch, leave, data export, delete/restore workspace. Obtains a PAT headless via POST /api/v1/auth/signin.

Journey: sign up and onboard

  1. /login: email-first form (login-email, login-continue); check-email routes to sign-in (password) or create account.
  2. New account: signup sends an email OTP, confirm verifies it. External-dependency step (email inbox); alternatives: magic link, GitHub/Google OAuth (third-party redirect).
  3. No membership: /onboarding, workspace name and slug.
  4. POST /api/v1/workspaces; creator becomes owner on community.
  5. Lands on /projects.

Branches: slug taken; wrong password; Supabase Auth rate limit (429 on auth routes). Data: business-data-context flow-onboarding.

Journey: author an ATC and execute a run

  1. Project explorer: create module, then user story (title, Markdown, optional Jira key).
  2. Add ACs, mark the story ready to test (needs an active AC).
  3. /projects/[slug]/atcs/new: steps, assertions, layer, tags, technique, priority; anchor to ACs of that story.
  4. /projects/[slug]/tests/new: chain ATCs from the workspace library, reorder, tag.
  5. Test detail: "Start run", pick an environment.
  6. Runner: mark each step; live updates via Realtime.
  7. Finish (verdict computed) or Abort (reason).
  8. Run history and project run report; coverage and traceability reflect the run.

Branches and failures: ATC without ACs or with foreign ACs rejected; closed run refuses marks; a run left idle 4 h is auto-aborted by the sweep (the runner page must then show the closed state); workspace deleted while the runner is open (BK-1129: no feedback today). Data: flow-story-atc, flow-test-run, state-run.

Journey: file and work a bug from a failed step

  1. In the runner, mark a step failed; "Report bug" appears (member+).
  2. Dialog pre-filled from the step; adjust severity, evidence links.
  3. Submit; server re-checks the step is still failed.
  4. Bug detail: assign to an active non-viewer member; move status forward one step at a time.
  5. Assignee gets in-app notifications (and the daily email digest if enabled).

Branches: step re-marked before submit (422); skip or reverse status rejected; viewer assignee rejected. Data: flow-bug-from-step, state-bug.

Journey: invite a teammate

  1. Admin or owner opens /workspaces/[id]/members, invites an email at viewer, member or admin.
  2. Invitee opens the accept link (may need to sign in first; external email step).
  3. Accept creates the membership at the invited role and redirects to /projects.

Branches: already a member at equal or higher rank; expired, revoked or deleted-workspace invite (same 404). Admin can resend or revoke. Data: flow-invite.

Journey: plan a test cycle

  1. /projects/[slug]/plans: create a Test Plan (name, goal, description).
  2. Plan detail /plans/[planId]: add Tests from the project, remove Tests.
  3. Edit while open.

Branches: duplicate name, over-length fields, empty selection, Test from another project, double submit. Closing a plan is not reachable (no close path found). Data: flow-test-plan.

Journey: import stories from Jira

  1. Project explorer: "Import from Jira", enter JQL.
  2. Dialog polls every 2 s until the job completes or fails.
  3. Imported stories appear in the tree (matching component module or "Inbox").

Branches: import already running (409); bad Jira credentials (job failed); partial per-issue errors. External dependency: the customer's Jira. Data: flow-jira-import.

Journey: upgrade to the Cloud plan

  1. /settings/billing: seat and project meters against the plan.
  2. /settings/billing/upgrade: choose seats, start checkout (admin or owner, browser session).
  3. Redirect to Stripe hosted Checkout (external-dependency step: card entry on Stripe).
  4. Return to Bunkai; plan becomes cloud once the webhook lands (asynchronous).

Money changes hands at step 3. Branches: second tab while a session is open; cancel; payment failed or session expired; project limit reached on community before upgrading (45700). Data: flow-billing-upgrade.

Journey: export workspace data

  1. Owner opens /settings/data-export, requests an export.
  2. Status shows queued, running, then ready (or failed).
  3. Download the archive within 7 days.

Branches: non-owner or PAT refused; second request while one is active; expired archive. Data: flow-workspace-export.

Journey: delete and restore a workspace

  1. Owner deletes the workspace from settings (browser session, confirmation).
  2. Everyone loses access at once; the workspace disappears from switchers and every deep link answers not found.
  3. Within 30 days the owner can restore from /workspaces/[id]/restore; after that it is purged.

Branches: non-owner refused; double submit; restore of a non-deleted workspace; members with the runner open (BK-1129). Data: flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace.

Cross-feature: traceability and coverage

Story, AC, ATC, Test, Run and Bug are authored in different features, but the traceability chain, coverage gaps, defect heatmap, recovery cycles and the Home widgets only make sense across all of them. A change in any one (an ATC edit, a run verdict, a bug status) must surface in the read views. Coverage counts skipped and blocked as not run (migration 0090).

Cross-feature: notifications

Runs (finished, aborted) and bugs (assigned, reassigned, status changed) emit activity rows that a trigger turns into inbox notifications, filtered by each member's preferences, and summarized daily by email. Testing a run or bug journey should check the recipient's inbox, not only the actor's screen.

Discovery gaps

  • No figures: tables and text carry every fact; the system architecture figure lives in infra-context (architecture). Draw a section figure only where a picture adds mechanism.
  • Role test accounts: STAGING_<ROLE>_EMAIL keys are optional (commented) in .env.example; whether each is populated in .env was not checked (the file is read-protected).
  • No route to remove another member or change a member's role; members page reads via SSR. Product gap or undiscovered Server Action.
  • No update or delete route for Projects, ATCs, Tests, Milestones or Test Plans.
  • Test Plan closing: status closed exists but no close path.
  • Account profile edit path (name, password) not traced.
  • Capabilities.tsx marks Test Plans, billing, inbox, preferences and Home as próximo: stale against shipped code.
  • Where the delete-workspace action sits in the UI (assumed /settings/workspaces) not confirmed.
  • Legacy .context/SRS/functional-specs.md was not re-read in full; rules here were re-derived from code and migrations.
